fun_facts: Mike Evans was a standout high-school basketball player in Galveston, Texas.
Mike Evans didn’t play football until his senior year of high school; he had dreams of playing both basketball and football professionally.

At Texas A&M in 2013, Mike Evans recorded a school-record 1,394 receiving yards and 12 touchdowns. He also broke the school single-game receiving record twice that season: first with 279 yards against Alabama, then with 287 against Auburn.
As a kid, Mike Evans watched Peyton Manning on TV while his mother cleaned the house.
Mike Evans started his NFL career with 11 consecutive 1,000-yard receiving seasons, tying Jerry Rice’s mark for the longest such streak.

excerpts:
**COLLEGE STATION, Texas --** Texas A&M receiver Mike Evans is declaring for the NFL draft.

Evans, a redshirt sophomore, was a consensus All-American and a Biletnikoff Award finalist this season.

He had 69 receptions for a school-record 1,394 yards and 12 touchdowns. He also set a school record with 279 yards receiving against Alabama this year. He broke his own record when he had 287 yards receiving against Auburn later in the season.

A 6-foot-5 former basketball star, Evans is rated as one of the top draft prospects at his position.

excerpts:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers receiver continued his career-long streak of 1,000-yard receiving seasons on Sunday [against](https://www.nfl.com/games/saints-at-buccaneers-2024-reg-18) the New Orleans Saints, hauling in a 9-yard pass in the final seconds of the fourth quarter from [Baker Mayfield](https://www.nfl.com/players/baker-mayfield) to surpass the mark for the 11th straight season. In the process, Evans tied Hall of Famer Jerry Rice for the most 1,000-yard receiving seasons consecutively.

Evans also extended his NFL record for most consecutive 1,000-yard campaigns to begin a career and edged closer to Rice’s all-time mark of 14 overall.
